prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Great question — “shadow work” is taught from very different angles (Jungian/depth psychology, somatic/trauma-informed therapy, New Age transformational workshops, and spiritual traditions like Buddhist or shamanic practice). Below I give vetted platforms and course-types to consider, recommended teachers/organizations to look for, safety tips, and a short starter plan so you can pick the best fit for your goals.

Top places to look (with why they’re worth considering)
- Jung Platform (jungplatform.com)
  - Strengths: Courses and recorded lectures by Jungian analysts and depth-psychology teachers focused on the shadow, dreams, archetypes, and active imagination. Good if you want theory + practical exercises grounded in Jungian tradition.
- C.G. Jung Institutes / Jung societies (local and online)
  - Strengths: High-quality, often clinician-led public lectures and certificate programs. Best for serious study and a clinical/depth-psychology approach.
- Sounds True (soundstrue.com)
  - Strengths: Hosts programs from reputable spiritual teachers and psychotherapists (meditation, embodiment, and some shadow-specific programs). Good for integration of spiritual practice with inner work.
- Insight Timer
  - Strengths: Lots of free and low-cost guided meditations and multi-session courses on shadow, self-inquiry, and integration from a wide array of teachers. Good for daily practice and experimentation.
- Coursera / edX / university extension programs
  - Strengths: Academic/psychology courses (e.g., personality, psychotherapy, Jungian theory through continuing ed). Good for grounding in psychology and research-based approaches.
- Udemy / Teachable / Skillshare
  - Strengths: Many inexpensive practical “how-to” shadow-work courses. Quality varies — read reviews and teacher credentials carefully.
- Sounds True / Gaia / Mindvalley (for transformational-style programs)
  - Strengths: Large-production programs emphasizing accelerated change and spiritual practices. Useful if you want a structured, motivational environment — but vet content and teacher credibility.

Reputable teachers & program types to search for
- James Hollis — Jungian analyst; clear, practical approach to shadow and midlife issues.
- Robert A. Johnson — classic short book “Owning Your Shadow”; look for recordings/lectures derived from his work.
- Robert Augustus Masters — psychotherapist who offers online trainings on shadow, intimacy, and boundaries (trauma-aware approach).
- Connie Zweig & Jeremiah Abrams — authors/teachers who have written classic shadow-work books; look for workshops they endorse.
- Tara Brach / Jack Kornfield / Sharon Salzberg — not specifically “shadow-only,” but their mindfulness and compassionate inquiry courses are excellent complement for spiritual practice and integration.

Safety, trauma, and integration — important cautions
- Shadow work often exposes painful memories, shame, or dissociation. If you have trauma, severe anxiety, active self-harm ideation, or major mental-health conditions, do this work with a licensed therapist or trauma-informed practitioner.
- Prefer courses that: (a) are trauma-aware, (b) offer community support (group or coach check-ins), and/or (c) give clear integration steps (grounding, somatic practices).
- Watch out for teachers who promise “instant transformation,” coercive group tactics, or patterns that discourage professional mental-health care.

Free/low-cost starter resources
- Guided meditations and short shadow courses on Insight Timer (search “shadow work,” “inner child,” “self-inquiry”).
- Introductory talks/webinars on Jung Platform (often free webinars).
- Read first: “Owning Your Shadow” (Robert A. Johnson) and “Meeting the Shadow” (editors Connie Zweig & Jeremiah Abrams) to get a clear conceptual frame before diving into intense exercises.
- Daily practice: journaling prompts (daily “what triggered me today?”), 10–20 min mindfulness/compassion meditations, and a “shadow inventory” worksheet (identify patterns, judgments, projections).

How to choose the best course for you (quick checklist)
- Goal alignment: therapeutic integration vs. spiritual initiation vs. intellectual study?
- Teacher credentials: clinician? Jungian analyst? experienced spiritual teacher?
- Trauma-sensitivity: does the course give grounding/somatic practices and referrals?
- Format: self-paced modules, live group coaching, or one-on-one mentoring?
- Community/support: is there a moderated group or access to teacher feedback?
- Trial/refund: is there a preview or guarantee to reduce risk?

A simple 4-week starter plan (doable without a full course)
- Week 1: Read a short primer (Owning Your Shadow), do 10 min daily mindfulness.
- Week 2: Daily journaling: triggers, judgments, recurring projections; 1 weekly guided shadow meditation.
- Week 3: Practice active imagination (10–15 min a few times): dialogue with a recurring inner figure; start body-grounding work after sessions.
- Week 4: Review patterns, make an integration plan (who to reach out to if it’s intense; small boundary/behavior changes to test).

If you want, tell me:
- Do you prefer a psychological/Jungian approach, a spiritually oriented teacher, or trauma-informed therapy-style work?
- Budget and whether you want self-paced or live group coaching?

I can then recommend 3–5 specific current courses or programs tailored to your needs and budget.
